To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

long-term temporal convoluted neural networks are more effective than short-term ones for action recognition, and that high-quality optical flow is essential for learning accurate action representations.

(a) LTC-CNN models are able to learn action representations at their full temporal extents; (b) LTC-CNNs outperform state-of-the-art methods for human action recognition on two challenging benchmarks; and (c) the quality of optical flow estimation is a crucial factor in the accuracy of action representations learned by LTC-CNNs.

long-term temporal convoluted neural networks (LTC) are able to learn action models with improved accuracy compared to the state-of-the-art methods and that the quality of the input optical flow fields is crucial for learning accurate action representations.
